_comment: Written LAST, from what building this skill by hand actually needed.
HANDOVER §0 item 11 says to build two skills by hand first and let the
format fall out of what they needed, rather than designing a schema and
then discovering it is wrong. Every field below earned its place by
being something the build could not do without. Nothing here is
speculative, and the fields a second skill turns out to need should be
name: Beat Montage
summary: Cuts a folder of footage to the beat of its own music bed, 9:16.
_toolApi: A DECLARED tool-API version, per §0 item 11. A skill is a recipe of
tool calls, and tools change: `detect_beats` gained `percussive` and
`import_media_from_path` gained `decoded` in the same session this was
written. A skill that ran against the old shapes has no way to know it
is now reading fields that do not exist unless it says which API it was
_template: The buyer can never get nothing (§6): if the agent fumbles, this is
still a real, playable project on the timeline — bed, tracks and a
title. It is also what makes the skill demoable before purchase.
It stores its media as ./assets/… so the folder can be installed
anywhere; verified by copying the whole directory elsewhere and opening
it there, where the bed still decoded at 119.6 BPM.

_licence: Assets are licensed PER SKILL, which is tractable, rather than per
library, which is not (§6). This one is synthesised, so the licence
is trivial — but the field exists because the next skill's will not
be, and a skill store cannot ask that question retroactively.

slots.description: A folder of clips. Ordered by filename unless you say otherwise.
The opening card. Leave empty to drop it.

_slots: What the buyer is allowed to change without editing the recipe. Both of
these are things the by-hand build had to be told, so they are the two
that exist. `targetClipName` is how a slot finds its clip in the
template, and it is a NAME rather than an id because ids are regenerated
_verify: The fourth part, and the one that makes this a skill rather than a
prompt pack. 12 checks, all against artifacts: the template opens with
its own assets and nobody else's, the cuts land on the bed's detected
beats (0ms worst), the frames on screen are the caller's footage in the
reported order (measured as colour distance, because a montage that
reported shots it never rendered is a thing that has happened here),
and the exported file is portrait, has an audio stream, and is the

_notInHereYet: Deliberately absent until a second skill proves they are needed:
no dependency graph between recipe steps (this one is a straight
line), no per-slot validation rules (the folder either has media or
assemble_from_folder says what it skipped), no pricing or entitlement
(that is the store, HANDOVER Stage 4 item 13, and a second product),
and no install/uninstall lifecycle — nothing installs skills yet, and
writing that format before something reads it is how you get a schema
